rules.mapping:
`cna_pbr_material_extensions_*` over an owned handle. The canonical type is a **value** -- it compares, hashes and prints by content -- but it holds nine borrowed `Texture2D` pointers, so it is bound as a handle rather than a C structure: a plain structure would put raw texture pointers in caller-writable memory. It never owns a texture given to it, which is the borrow rule this ABI already settled for effects. `copy_from` exists because a handle cannot be assigned and the canonical type is copyable; the texture members are copied as borrows.

`operator==` and `operator!=` map to the single `_equals` route, and texture members compare **by identity** -- two sets are equal when they point at the same textures, not at equal ones. `GetHashCode` widens to `uint64_t`, the campaign's settled deviation. `ToString` takes the count/copy form and names only the active extensions, so a neutral set prints as two bytes.

**This type throws nowhere: all twenty-four setters correct, in three different shapes, and telling them apart is the whole contract.** Nine members clamp to zero-to-one (`std::clamp`, per channel for the three colours). Five use a **guarded assignment** -- `if (value >= bound) field = value;` -- which leaves the previous value in place, so an out-of-range write is a silent no-op rather than a value pinned to the bound; four guard at zero and `iridescenceIor` guards at **one**, because an index of refraction below one describes a medium light speeds up in. One, `attenuationDistance`, floors at zero with a ternary, writing the bound where its neighbours keep the old value. Nine texture members take no correction at all.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 20, which writes every scalar out of range at both ends and reads it back, so each of the three correction shapes is distinguished from the other two rather than assumed; asserts the colour clamps element-wise; round-trips a borrowed texture and proves binding one does not keep it alive; and checks equality, hash and `ToString` against a copy that is then made to differ by one field. Proved to execute by asserting the guarded setter clamps to zero and watching the exit code move to stage 20.

rules.mapping: `cna_thin_film_iridescence_evaluate` and `_copy_glsl`. Both canonical members are static and the class holds no state, so neither needs a handle and no object kind is added. `evaluate` clamps its cosine to zero-to-one and floors each result channel at zero, both **corrections** carried through unchanged; `getGlsl` takes the count/copy form.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 20, which asserts a cosine past one gives the same answer as one -- the only way the clamp is observable from C -- refuses a null reflectance, and reads the GLSL through the count/copy pair.

rules.mapping:
The material itself was already bound by `CBIND-035F7` as two fixed-layout PODs: the frozen `CNA_PbrMaterial`, whose layout cannot change within an ABI major, and the versioned `CNA_PbrMaterialEXT`, which carries every canonical field. `CBIND-087B` binds what a POD alone cannot express -- the value semantics -- as `cna_pbr_material_ext_equals`, `_get_hash_code` and `_copy_to_string`, plus `kPbrTextureSlotCount` as `CNA_PBR_TEXTURE_SLOT_COUNT` and the `PbrTextureSlot` identities, each tied to its canonical ordinal by a `static_assert`.

**Every canonical setter here is a bare assignment**, the exact opposite of `PbrMaterialExtensions` beside it, and reading the bodies is the only thing that establishes that -- there is no idiom to grep for when a setter corrects nothing.

**The one correction in the canonical type never reaches C, and the POD mapping is why.** `getTextureCoordinateSet` and `getTextureTransform` take a `PbrTextureSlot` and route it through an `IndexOf` that folds an out-of-range slot onto base colour. The C form carries both as fixed arrays of `CNA_PBR_TEXTURE_SLOT_COUNT` inside the structure, so there is no slot argument to validate and no fold to reproduce: an out-of-range index is the caller's own array bounds error, not something this ABI can silently redirect. That is a deviation worth stating rather than a gap -- the POD mapping removes a surprise the enum mapping would have had to carry.

The three value routes are gated on the engine layer together, even though the structure is describable in either build, because they answer with the canonical rule. Splitting them -- reimplementing equality field by field in C while the hash stayed gated -- would make equality answerable in a build where the hash consistent with it is not.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 21, which changes each field the canonical type gained after `CNA_PbrMaterial` was frozen **one at a time** and requires the pair to stop matching, walks every one of the seven slots in both per-slot arrays rather than only the first, requires a changed field to change the hash (without which equal-hash-for-equal-values is vacuous), and refuses a malformed structure. The layer-absent build asserts all three routes report `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED` and write nothing. Proved to execute by inverting the hash assertion and watching the exit code move to stage 21.

rules.mapping: `CNA_TransparencyMode` with its three constants at the canonical ordinals, tied to the canonical enumerators by a `static_assert`. A pure identity, so it needs no object and the constants are readable in either build.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 21, which asserts the three are contiguous from zero in canonical order

rules.mapping:
The `cna_effect_*_ext` routes `CBIND-085B1` bound. The shadow-receiver contract is an interface, and this campaign binds an interface as operations on the implementing object's handle -- resolved by `dynamic_cast` and refused **by argument** rather than by handle when the effect does not implement it. These thirty-two rows are the two PBR effects' `override` of that interface, so no new route belongs here: what the slice owes is evidence that the existing routes actually resolve these two types.

That is not a formality. Both effects live in `modules/graphics` rather than the engine layer, so they exist in builds where the routes that drive them do not, and a route that resolved for `BasicEffect` while silently refusing a `PbrEffect` would leave every PBR shadow inert with no error a caller could see.

Four rows are deferred with named owners: `set`/`getImageBasedLightEXT` on both effects take an `ImageBasedLightEXT`, which `CBIND-091` owns.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 22, which runs every member of the receiver contract against a `PbrEffect` and a `SkinnedPbrEffect` and **reads each value back** -- the difference between the cast succeeding and the call being accepted and dropped. Stage 13 already covers `BasicEffect` and the refusal of a `SpriteEffect` that implements nothing. Proved to execute by asserting the wrong filter radius and watching the exit code move to stage 22.

rules.mapping:
`cna_gltf_material_bridge_build_material` and `_build_extensions`, over four versioned PODs: `CNA_GltfMaterialTexturesEXT`, `CNA_GltfMaterialExtensionTexturesEXT` and the two source structures with their `_init` routines.

**The canonical bridge is written against a C++20 *concept*, not a type**, so that the importer's own record satisfies it without this layer knowing that record. A concept has no C form and is not a callable operation, so the C bridge takes a structure that names exactly the members each concept requires, and the implementation builds a local type from it to meet the constraint. The concept stays the contract; the structure is how C reaches it.

**One value is not carried exactly, and that is canonical rather than a limit of the binding:** glTF's `baseColorFactor` is four floats and a material's albedo is a `Color`, so it is quantised to eight bits per channel. Everything else round-trips. The `_init` routines fill the glTF specification's own defaults -- 1.0 metallic and roughness, 1.5 IOR, 0.5 alpha cutoff -- not this layer's, because an omitted glTF factor means the specification's value.

Textures are borrowed, never owned. An undefined alpha mode is refused rather than cast through into the material, the same rule every enum identity in this ABI follows.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 23, which asserts the glTF defaults rather than this layer's, sees the base-colour quantisation with a fractional value (1.0 would survive any quantiser), refuses a malformed structure and an undefined alpha mode, and builds extensions whose transmission predicate then reports true. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses, the two `_init` routines included -- a caller that can fill a source but not use it has been told nothing useful.

rules.mapping:
`cna_transparent_draw_list_*` over an owned handle; a pure CPU object that touches no device. `submit` takes a `CNA_TransparentDrawCallback` and a context in place of the canonical `std::function`, following the campaign's callback convention.

**The class has exactly one refusal and it is a contract:** an entry with nothing to draw is a caller mistake, so a null callback is refused at submission rather than stored and discovered when the draw runs. A failing callback stops `draw_sorted` and **its own result reaches the caller unchanged**, so a caller learns which draw failed instead of finding a partly drawn frame; the failure travels as a private exception across the canonical `std::function` and is unwrapped at the boundary rather than being flattened by the firewall.

`drawSorted` and `getSortedOrderEXT` take a **view matrix**, not a camera position, matching the canonical signature rather than asking a caller to derive the position twice. `sortKey` measures to the **nearest point of the box**, so a camera inside a box keys at zero.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 23, which submits near-first and requires the sorted order to reverse it, asserts the zero key for a camera inside the box (a centre-distance implementation would pass a test that only compared two disjoint boxes), refuses a null callback and null bounds without changing the count, and proves a failing callback stops the draw at the first entry and returns its own result.

rules.mapping:
`cna_weighted_blended_transparency_*` over an owned handle. Both targets are borrowed and exist exactly when the resolve does.

**The eight canonical throws are two different mistakes and are kept apart.** `invalid_argument` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and `logic_error` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`, because a caller acts on them differently: fix the number, or fix the order of the calls. Flattening them -- which the firewall would do unaided -- would tell a caller that a size of zero and a bracket left open are the same error. Both are checked ahead of the canonical call so the result is decided here rather than recovered from an exception type.

`weight` clamps twice, and both are **corrections**: the curve is unbounded near zero depth, and a weight that overflows would poison the whole accumulation buffer rather than one fragment.

**`begin` opens the bracket only where the resolve is supported**, so on a renderer without it `isAccumulating` stays false and the matching `end` refuses. That is canonical behaviour, **reproduced rather than corrected** -- see `CBIND-098`, which records it as a defect with a reproduction rather than fixing engine-layer code from a binding slice.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 23, which asserts the argument and state refusals are different results, exercises every sequencing mistake while the bracket is open, and branches on `is_supported` so **both** the opening and the non-opening path assert -- the non-opening one pins `CBIND-098` in place, so a later fix shows up as a test that must change. Proved to execute on both branches by inverting the accumulating assertion and watching the exit code move to stage 23 on EasyGL and on HEADLESS alike.

rules.mapping:
A versioned `CNA_RenderPipelineSettingsEXT` carrying all forty-seven fields, beside the frozen ten-field `CNA_RenderPipelineSettings` that `CBIND-035F7` bound and whose layout cannot change within an ABI major -- the `CNA_PbrMaterialEXT` precedent, applied for the same reason. `kMinimumGamma` and `kMinimumFxaaEdgeThreshold` become macros with a `static_assert`; `applyRenderQualityPresetEXT` and `applyFromStringEXT` become routes.

**The row that planned this slice proposed a plain POD because the type is "almost all fields". Reading the bodies contradicted that.** Thirty-one of the forty-seven setters correct their input: ten clamp to a two-sided range and twenty-one floor at a minimum, across six distinct bounds -- `0..0.5`, `0..1`, `0..0.25`, `0..0.1`, `0`, and the two named minima. Twenty-one of those use an `AtLeast` helper that a grep for `clamp` does not find, the blind spot `CBIND-087A` recorded.

**So the structure is a description, not the stored state.** Every conversion to the canonical type runs each field through its canonical setter, which is what preserves the corrections a plain structure copy would lose, and `_normalize` performs that round trip in place so a caller can ask what the engine will actually store. Writing `5.0` into a field the setter clamps to `0.1` is not an error and is not silently honoured -- it becomes `0.1`, and the route that shows you so is part of the binding rather than an afterthought.

The sixteen fields that correct nothing stay uncorrected on purpose: the canonical source states that the passes clamp what they apply, and a settings bag that clamped to one pass's limits would silently change the number a caller reads back. Undefined identities and out-of-contract booleans are refused rather than cast through.

**Twenty-two rows stay with `CBIND-035F7`** -- the class, its constructor and the ten fields the frozen structure already carries. They are bound, by direct field access on that structure, and this slice does not restate them. Worth knowing, and recorded on `CBIND-088A`: direct field access on the **frozen** structure does not apply the corrections, so a caller writing `gamma = 0` there holds a value the canonical setter would have floored. The `EXT` structure carries the same ten fields and does normalize them, which is the route new code should take.
rules.tests:
`EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 24, which writes every corrected field out of range in both directions and asserts **its own** bound -- thirty-one separate expectations rather than one shared range -- and requires each floor to leave a large value untouched, which is what separates a floor from a clamp. The quality preset is proved to do something by requiring Low and Ultra to disagree. The serialized-text route is exercised with the canonical `;` separator, an unrecognised field that must be skipped rather than refused, and an embedded NUL that must be refused because it would silently truncate what a caller believes it applied. The layer-absent build asserts all four routes refuse and write nothing.

Proved to execute, and proved to discriminate: asserting the common `0..1` bound for the one field clamped to `0..0.1` moves the exit code to stage 24, which is exactly the mistake a single shared expectation would have shipped.

rules.mapping:
`cna_render_pipeline_*` over an owned handle, with `FrameStatistics` as a versioned `CNA_RenderPipelineFrameStatisticsEXT`. Settings are copied in and out through `CNA_RenderPipelineSettingsEXT` -- the canonical getter returns a reference into the pipeline and the C form copies, so the result stays correct after the pipeline changes; writing them back runs every field through its canonical setter, so `CBIND-088A`'s thirty-one corrections apply here unchanged.

**The frame bracket was read before the test was written, because two other classes in this phase are not what they look like.** `RenderPipeline::begin` marks the frame open *before* any support check and `end` clears it *before* any early return, so the pair is symmetric on every renderer -- unlike `WeightedBlendedTransparency` (`CBIND-098`) and the shadow maps (`CBIND-097`). Both halves can therefore assert success rather than branching on support. A negative finding, but only because it was checked.

**Six throws, two kinds, and one pair the exception type cannot separate.** `invalid_argument` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (a non-positive size, an inverted or non-positive camera plane pair) and `logic_error` becomes `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`. But `begin` throws `logic_error` for **two different states** -- a frame already open, and a pipeline that has never been sized -- and the pipeline exposes no width accessor to tell them apart after the fact. The C layer therefore remembers whether `resize` ever succeeded and answers the two with their own messages, which is work the binding does rather than something it inherits.

Both callback surfaces follow `CBIND-087D`'s rule: a failing draw stops the frame and its own result reaches the caller unchanged. The user pass and the shadow map are borrowed, never owned. Three rows are deferred with named owners: `setSkybox`/`getSkybox` to `CBIND-091`, which owns `Skybox`, and `getPassTimingsEXT` to `CBIND-089`, which owns `PostProcessChain::PassTiming`.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 25, which drives the whole frame lifecycle and asserts the two `begin` states separately -- never-sized before `resize`, already-open after a successful `begin` -- refuses releasing device resources mid-frame, proves an out-of-range setting written through the pipeline comes back corrected, and cross-checks every statistic against its individual accessor so a copy-paste error between the two readings shows up. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. Proved to execute on both arms by asserting that a never-sized pipeline accepts `begin`, which moves the exit code to stage 25.

rules.mapping:
`cna_post_process_chain_*` over an owned handle. The target pool is a **counted borrow**: destroying the chain is refused while the pool handle is outstanding.

**`addOwnedPass` is the one route in the engine layer that consumes a handle a caller still holds, and the reason is worth stating.** The canonical signature takes a `std::unique_ptr`; this ABI holds its objects in `shared_ptr` and cannot release one, so a literal transfer is not expressible. Rather than fake it, the chain resource keeps the handed-over pass alive itself and registers it with the non-owning `addPass`. **The observable lifetime is identical** -- the pass lives exactly as long as the chain, `clear` releases it, and the caller's handle is released either way -- and it avoids the one thing a forced transfer risks, two owners of the same object. The route is named `add_owned_pass` rather than being a flag on `add_pass` precisely because the handle dies; a caller can see that in the name.

`PassTiming` carries a name, a duration and a sample count. A C structure cannot own the string, so the timing splits into a plain `CNA_PassTimingEXT` value and a separate `copy_pass_timing_name` -- the structure then has no lifetime of its own. Both canonical throws on `apply` are argument mistakes and are answered before the chain sees them, with separate messages: a context with no source has nothing to read from, and a non-positive size gives the chain nothing to allocate its intermediates against.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 26, which proves the borrowed pass stays usable after the chain records it and the **owned** pass's handle is genuinely dead afterwards -- asserted rather than documented, because a route promising ownership transfer that left the handle usable would invite a double free. It also refuses an index into an empty timing list, and asserts the pool borrow blocks destruction. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses. Proved to execute on both arms by asserting the consumed handle still answers, which moves the exit code to stage 26.

rules.mapping: `cna_render_pipeline_get_pass_timing_count_ext`, `_get_pass_timing_ext` and `_copy_pass_timing_name_ext`. `CBIND-088B` deferred this row here because its return type is `PostProcessChain::PassTiming`, which this slice defines; one canonical getter returning a vector of records with strings becomes three routes for the reason the chain's own timings do.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 26, which reads the count and refuses an index past it

rules.mapping:
One `cna_<pass>_create` each, plus the accessors the pass alone knows. Everything the three share -- `apply`, `getName`, `isSupported`, destruction -- is already bound by `CBIND-084` on the `CNA_PostProcessPassHandle`, so those rows map to routes that exist rather than to new ones. **A pass-specific accessor is refused by argument, not by handle, when the handle names another pass**: the handle is perfectly valid, it is the concrete type that cannot answer, which is the rule `CBIND-085B1` settled for interfaces.

Two internal helpers carry the shape for the rest of the phase: `CreateEnginePass<T>` and `WithEnginePass<T>`. `CBIND-089C` and `CBIND-089D` reuse them unchanged, which is what makes thirteen more passes a table rather than thirteen more designs.

**Three correction shapes, and the bounds differ between fields of the same pass.** `SsrPass` clamps its roughness blur to `0..0.25` and its edge fade to `0..0.5`, and guards three more with `if (value > 0)`, which leaves the previous value in place rather than pinning to the bound. `DepthOfFieldPass` guards three and clamps one. **`SsaoPass` corrects nothing at all** -- established by reading the four setter bodies, not by the file-level grep, which counted five corrections in that file that all live in `apply()` rather than in a setter. That is the same blind spot `CBIND-087A` recorded, in the opposite direction: a grep that over-counts is as misleading as one that under-counts.

`kMinStepCount`/`kMaxStepCount` become macros, and the setter deliberately does **not** enforce them: the march clamps the count where it applies it, so a caller reads back what it wrote. That is the canonical convention this campaign has now met three times -- the passes clamp what they apply, so the settings never silently change a number a caller can read.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 27, which asserts **each bound on its own** -- proved to matter by asserting the edge fade clamps to its neighbour's 0.25 instead of its own 0.5, which moves the exit code to stage 27 on both arms. Each guarded setter gets the extra half a clamp does not need: a valid value first, then an out-of-range write that must leave the valid one in place. The free fields are written out of range and must survive, the step count past its own documented maximum. The packed and unpacked occlusion GLSL must differ, or the flag is ignored; Low and Ultra must ask for different sample counts, or the preset does nothing; and the circle of confusion must be exactly zero at the focus distance and grow away from it in both directions. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses.

rules.mapping:
One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s `CreateEnginePass<T>`/`WithEnginePass<T>` helpers reused unchanged -- which is what makes four more passes a table rather than four more designs. The shared base stays with `CBIND-084`; the three per-pass constants become macros with a `static_assert`.

**The guards here are not interchangeable, and that is the whole slice.** Four setters guard with `if (value >= 0)` and **accept zero** -- no fog, no shafts and no aerial perspective are all legitimate settings -- while `VolumetricFogPass::setRange` and `HeightFogPass::setFalloff` guard with `if (value > 0)` and **reject zero as well**, because a zero range has no volume to march and a zero falloff is a division by zero. A shared "negatives are ignored" reading would have got two of the six wrong.

Two more bounds are unusual enough to name. `setTurbidity` floors at **one**, not zero: turbidity is a ratio against a perfectly clear atmosphere, so below one describes air clearer than vacuum. `setAnisotropy` clamps to **-0.95 through 0.95** -- the only two-sided clamp in this phase with a negative lower bound, because scattering runs from fully backward to fully forward and both poles are singular. `HeightFogPass::setBaseHeight` corrects nothing, because a fog base below the origin is legitimate.

`setLight` takes a borrowed shadow map; `CNA_INVALID_HANDLE` means march unshadowed rather than being an error.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 28, which asserts each guard's own bound -- a valid value, then zero, then a negative -- so the `>= 0` and `> 0` guards are told apart rather than assumed alike. Proved to matter by asserting the range guard admits zero the way the density beside it does, which moves the exit code to stage 28 on both arms. The three pure functions are checked by their **relationships** rather than by duplicating their maths: air mass grows with distance, transmittance falls as air mass grows, and optical depth is exactly zero at zero distance and grows with both distance and density. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses.

rules.mapping:
One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers.

**Two of the nine are not passes, and finding that out was the slice.** `DecalPass` and `SpatialUpscalePass` are named "Pass" and were counted among the seventeen, but neither derives from `PostProcessPass`: they have no `apply`, and each is driven by its own `draw` with explicit sizes rather than by a chain. The compiler said so -- their `shared_ptr` would not convert -- which is the only reason it was caught before the shape was wrong in the ABI. They carry their own handles (`CNA_DecalPassHandle`, `CNA_SpatialUpscalePassHandle`), their own object kinds and their own destroy, and the shared `cna_post_process_pass_*` routes correctly **refuse** them.

`AsciiPass::getEffect` lends the pass's own effect. Binding it needed the resource type behind `CNA_AsciiPostProcessEffectHandle` to be **shared between two translation units** rather than redeclared: two units that register or read one `ObjectKind` must agree on the type it holds, and a second local declaration would compile, register under the same kind, and then be cast to the wrong type -- undefined behaviour no test would reliably catch. `AsciiEffectResource` moved to `CnaCApiGraphicsExtDetail.hpp` for that reason, which is a deliberate structural change rather than a side effect.

**`FxaaPass` corrects nothing**, while the settings bag that can drive the same number floors it at `CNA_RENDER_PIPELINE_MINIMUM_FXAA_EDGE_THRESHOLD_EXT`. Two surfaces, one value, only one correcting -- asserted on both rather than assumed consistent. `DecalPass::setCamera` ignores a non-positive far plane by guarding the whole assignment, so the previous camera survives.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 29, which asserts the shared pass routes **refuse** the two standalone objects and accept the seven real passes -- the only way a caller learns the difference from outside. Proved to execute by asserting the shared destroy accepts a `DecalPass`, which moves the exit code to stage 29 on both arms. Every correcting field is written out of range at both ends against its own bound; `FxaaPass`'s free field is checked against the settings bag's floor in the same stage. The ASCII effect borrow is taken, released, and the pass then still answers. The layer-absent build asserts every route refuses.

rules.mapping:
One `cna_<pass>_create` each plus the pass's own accessors, on `CBIND-089B`'s helpers; both derive from `PostProcessPass`, so the shared routes drive them.

**`TonemapPass` corrects nothing** -- exposure and gamma are stored as given. `tonemapChannel` is the only way from C to see what a mode does to a value without rendering a frame, so it is bound as a free route.

**`ColorGradePass::setLut` was mis-read once and the run corrected it.** A regex over `if (…)` reported a guarded assignment; the body is an early return that *unbinds*, followed by a `throw` for a strip whose width is not the square of its height. So a null handle unbinds like every other `set*` in this ABI, and a malformed strip is **refused rather than sampled** -- one read at the wrong slice count grades the frame into colours nothing in the table names, which looks almost right and is therefore worse than an error. `setVolumeLut` refuses a non-cube or an edge outside two through `kMaxLutSize` for the same reason.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 31, which walks every tonemapping mode through `tonemapChannel` and requires `NONE` and `ACES` to disagree above one, asserts a null LUT unbinds and a 5-by-3 texture is refused, and refuses every undefined identity.

rules.mapping:
`cna_hdr_display_output_*` over its own handle -- it does not derive from `PostProcessPass`, established by the inheritance survey this slice ran **before** writing anything rather than by the compiler afterwards, which is what `CBIND-089D` cost.

**`setPeakNits` floors against another field, not a constant.** A peak below diffuse white would make white brighter than the brightest thing the display can show, so the bound is the current paper-white -- and it *moves* when paper-white does. It is the only correction of this shape in the engine layer, and no fixed expectation can describe it.

The five static functions are pure and bound as free routes: PQ encode/decode, Rec.709 to Rec.2020, the highlight roll-off, and the whole-colour encode.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 31, which sets two different paper-white values and requires the peak floor to land on each in turn -- proved to matter by asserting a fixed floor instead, which moves the exit code to stage 31 on both arms. PQ is checked by round-trip, the roll-off by requiring a huge input to stay under the peak, and Rec.2020 by requiring white to stay white, none of which restates the curves.

rules.mapping:
`cna_auto_exposure_ext_*` over its own handle. **It needs compute shaders and says so at construction**, not through an `is_supported` query: the canonical constructor builds a compute program and a storage buffer, so where the renderer has neither there is no object to create and `create` answers `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED`. That makes it the only object in the layer whose capability boundary is at creation, and the second compute-gated type after `CBIND-084A`'s.

**All four setters refuse; none of them ignores.** A regex over `if (…)` reported guarded assignments, and the run corrected it -- every one throws `invalid_argument`. Two are validated **as pairs**, so one good value and one bad writes neither. And `setExposure` both refuses *and* corrects: a non-positive value is refused, and an accepted one is then clamped into the current range, so a value inside the contract can still come back different.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 31, which asks the device for compute support and requires `create` to answer accordingly, then -- where the meter exists -- asserts each refusal leaves the previous value in place, that a good speed paired with a bad one writes neither, and that an accepted exposure above the range comes back clamped.

rules.mapping:
`cna_cube_lut_*` over its own handle, taking a `CNA_StringView` rather than a path-or-text guess. **This is the engine layer's only byte-facing surface**: everything else in Phase B9 takes numbers a caller chose, and this takes text a caller may have downloaded.

Its ten canonical throws all become `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT` -- they are all one thing to a caller, "these bytes are not a .cube file" -- with one exception kept apart: a file that cannot be opened is `CNA_RESULT_IO`, because a caller acts on that differently. `getEntry` refuses an index outside the table rather than clamping, since a clamped index returns a different colour and the frame would look almost right.
rules.tests: Two ways, because the release gate requires it of a parser-like surface (`CBIND-040B`). `CApi_CubeLutOracle` compares against an **independent oracle that emits where the parser scans** -- they run in opposite directions and share no code, and the expected entry is a closed form of its index so the comparison does not depend on the emitter's bookkeeping either. Every entry of every accepted size is compared, and one malformed case per refusal is enumerated. **Verified to catch a real disagreement rather than merely to run**: swapping red and blue in the parser's index arithmetic -- the classic `.cube` ordering mistake -- makes it exit 1 naming entry (1,0,0) at every size. `tests/fuzz/CubeLutFuzz.cpp` covers what enumeration cannot reach, and judges the answer rather than the absence of a crash: every accepted table must report a size within the documented bounds, read its corners, refuse one index past the edge, and release. `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 31 covers the layer-absent refusals.

rules.mapping: `CNA_DisplayColorSpace` and `CNA_LutInterpolation` with their constants at the canonical ordinals, and **`CNA_TONEMAPPING_MODE_UNCHARTED2`**, which `CBIND-088A` found declared canonically but absent from the C identity -- so a C caller could not select it and the settings validator refused its ordinal. Adding the macro and widening that bound are one change: `CBIND-088A` deliberately left the bound at three because the fifth identity had no C name, and widening it without one would have accepted an ordinal nobody could spell.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 31, which selects Uncharted2 on the pass and normalizes it through the settings bag, and refuses every ordinal past it

rules.mapping:
`cna_light_probe_ext_*` over its own owned handle. The probe is a value in C++ and stays a value here: `cna_light_probe_ext_copy_from` and `cna_light_probe_ext_equals` exist so a caller can do through the handle what assignment and comparison do through the object, and `cna_light_probe_volume_ext_set_probe` **copies** rather than borrows -- a volume that aliased its source would change under a caller who later scaled that probe.

The nine-coefficient table is reached one entry at a time and in bulk (`cna_light_probe_ext_copy_coefficients`, which reports the count it needs when the buffer is too small). `kCoefficientCount` and the six visibility directions become `CNA_LIGHT_PROBE_COEFFICIENT_COUNT_EXT` and `CNA_LIGHT_PROBE_VISIBILITY_DIRECTIONS_EXT`, and every index route refuses an index outside its table rather than clamping: a clamped index answers with a *different* coefficient, so the surface lights almost right, which is worse than an error.

Two behaviours read like refusals and are not, and are bound as answers because that is what the bodies do. `visibilityWeight` answers **1.0** -- "nothing known to be in the way" -- both when the probe carries no visibility data and when the distance is not positive; and the two visibility distances are floored at zero rather than refused. `irradiance` is likewise clamped non-negative however the coefficients reconstruct.

The two comparison operators map to the same `cna_light_probe_ext_equals` -- `operator!=` is its negation, and a separate route for "not equal" would be a second name for one answer.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 32: every coefficient round-trips, both ends of both index ranges are refused, the two not-refusals above are asserted as successes returning 1.0, a copy compares equal until one `scale` breaks it, and a probe written into a volume is shown not to follow its source. The layer-absent build asserts each route refuses and leaves its output untouched. The two operators are covered by the same equality assertions, in both directions.

rules.mapping:
`cna_light_probe_volume_ext_*` over its own owned handle. The canonical constructor throws three different `invalid_argument`s -- a count below one, a probe product over `CNA_LIGHT_PROBE_VOLUME_MAX_PROBES_EXT`, and an inverted bounding box -- and each is bound as its own refusal with its own message rather than folded into one, because a caller fixes them in three different ways.

`sampleProbe` **clamps** a position into the box instead of refusing it: a point just outside a probe grid is ordinary during rendering, and the canonical body treats it that way. `contains` is the query that answers the question refusing would have answered.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 32: the three construction refusals are asserted separately, the probe grid is indexed at both ends of all three axes, `contains` is checked inside and outside, and sampling from outside the box is asserted to **succeed**. The layer-absent build asserts each route refuses and leaves its output untouched.

rules.mapping:
`CNA_ImageBasedLightEXT`, a versioned POD carrying the three split-sum textures as handles plus the mip count and intensity, with `cna_image_based_light_ext_init` and `cna_image_based_light_ext_is_valid`.

Those two routes are the only engine-layer surface in this slice that lives **outside** `#ifdef CNA_CNAEXT`, because the canonical type does too: it is deliberately in the always-compiled XNA header rather than under the flag (`plans/plan_modern.md` `MOD-1222`). They therefore read their defaults from the canonical type instead of repeating them as literals, and they succeed in both builds -- refusing them would be as wrong as running the object routes.

`IsValidEXT()` maps arm for arm, including the one a handle rewrite invites you to drop: all three textures present **and** the mip count at least one **and the intensity not negative**. Here "present" is "a live texture handle", since a stale handle is not a texture and must not read as a complete bundle.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 32 and the layer-absent block: a default-initialized light reads **invalid** (a bundle with no textures is not two thirds of an answer), a negative intensity reads invalid, a short `struct_size` is refused, and both routes are asserted to succeed in the layer-absent build with the same answers.

rules.mapping:
The four effect-side operations that were waiting on the types above. `cna_effect_get_image_based_light_ext` / `cna_effect_set_image_based_light_ext` are one pair over `CNA_EffectHandle`, refusing **by argument** through a `dynamic_cast` rather than by handle kind, so the same pair serves both PBR effects; the two forward-effect routes take a probe handle and a volume handle.

The lifetime differs between them and is documented rather than smoothed over: the probe is **copied** into the effect, the volume is **borrowed**, and the textures the getter hands back alias the effect resource -- each keeps the effect alive while it exists, and releasing one releases only the handle, never the texture.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 32, which sets and reads back a bundle on both PBR effects and asserts the pair refuses an effect that implements neither; the layer-absent build asserts all four refuse.

rules.mapping:
`cna_light_probe_baker_*` over its own owned handle, with the canonical `SceneDraw` becoming `CNA_LightProbeSceneDrawCallback` -- a function pointer plus a `void*` context, the shape every other callback in this ABI uses.

**Whether a baker can bake is probed, not asked**, and the binding preserves that: no renderer publishes "can bind an offscreen target and read it back", and the two do not come together, so the canonical constructor renders one capture and remembers the result. The bake routes refuse an unsupported renderer with `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE` rather than `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED`, because the layer *is* present and the arguments *are* fine -- NOT_SUPPORTED would collide with "built without the layer" and send a caller to look at its build flags.

A null callback is refused **before** the support check and on every renderer: a bake that draws nothing produces a perfectly valid probe, and a caller could not tell it from a mistake. `setPlanes` is validated and refused as a **pair**, with no clamping -- a silently corrected capture range gives probes that look plausible and are lit from the wrong depth.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 33, which runs **both arms keyed on the measured support**: EasyGL takes the success path and counts six callback invocations per probe (twelve for a two-probe volume), headless takes the refusal path and asserts nothing was drawn. Four bad plane pairs are refused and both halves shown unchanged afterwards; the six faces are refused at both ends. Break-proved in both directions.

rules.mapping:
`cna_environment_processor_*` over its own owned handle. A pure transformer with **no setters at all**, so its nine argument refusals are each about one call rather than about accumulated state. Each generator hands back a new **owned** texture handle that outlives the processor.

**The generators are renderer-dependent and this type publishes no support flag to ask first** -- they build a real `TextureCube` and write its faces, which a renderer without cube storage refuses. That reaches a caller as `CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED`, the canonical answer, deliberately not rewritten. The header therefore documents the resulting ambiguity and how to resolve it (`cna_engine_layer_get_version`), and records that **the split is by output type**: the three cube-producing routes refuse while `generate_brdf_lut`, which builds a 2D table, still works.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 34. The five static maths routes are asserted as closed forms -- including that `hammersley` returns the texel **centre** `(index + 0.5) / count` rather than `index / count`, and that a mip count of one or less answers mip zero rather than refusing. The object routes branch on the measured answer and assert both arms; on the refusing renderer the stage additionally asserts the layer version is non-zero, which is the very distinction the header tells a caller to draw. Break-proved: breaking the headless-only arm moves only that tree.

rules.mapping:
`cna_skybox_*` over its own owned handle. Support is probed at construction, and a skybox that cannot draw -- refused shader, or no environment -- **skips silently and still succeeds**: a missing sky is a scene without a sky, not a broken frame.

Two attach routes, because the canonical class has two. `set_environment` **borrows** (and releases an owned cube first, or attaching over one would keep it alive with nothing referring to it); `set_owned_environment` **consumes the handle**, following `cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass`, the campaign's settled shape for a canonical `unique_ptr` parameter. The transfer is done by releasing the handle -- the last step that can fail, so a refusal never leaves the caller holding nothing -- and retaining the cube on the resource.

`setIntensity` **floors at zero**, which is deliberately *not* what the identically named `AtmosphericSky` setter does.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 35: drawing with nothing attached is asserted to **succeed**, the borrowed getter handle is released twice over to show the cube survives it, and the consumed handle is asserted to be unusable afterwards. The floor is asserted against the atmospheric sky's guard in the same stage, so a binding that regularized the two would fail exactly one of them.

rules.mapping:
`cna_atmospheric_sky_*` over its own owned handle, plus the pipeline's skybox pair that was waiting for `Skybox` to exist in C.

**Its three setters behave three different ways and the binding preserves each rather than regularizing them**: turbidity is clamped to one through ten; intensity is a *guarded assignment* that keeps the previous value on a negative; the sun direction is a guarded assignment that also *normalizes*, so what reads back is never what was written, and a vector too short to have a direction is a silent no-op. The free `radiance` function deliberately does **not** clamp its turbidity, unlike the setter -- the setter guards a sky drawn many times, the function evaluates what it is handed.

The pipeline's skybox is borrowed as the canonical pointer is, but the pipeline resource retains it anyway, so releasing the skybox handle mid-frame cannot leave a dangling pointer inside a live pipeline.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 35: each of the three setter shapes is asserted with a value that discriminates it from the other two, the turbidity clamp at both ends, the normalize-and-keep behaviour of the sun direction, and the pipeline pair round-tripping the caller's own handle.

rules.mapping:
`CNA_AreaLightEXT`, a versioned POD, with `CNA_AreaLightShapeEXT` and its three constants at the canonical ordinals, plus `cna_area_light_ext_init` and `cna_area_light_ext_is_valid`.

Like `CNA_ImageBasedLightEXT`, the canonical type is deliberately in the **always-compiled** XNA header rather than under `CNA_CNAEXT` (`plans/plan_modern.md` `MOD-1222`), so both value routes work in **every** build and read their defaults from the canonical type instead of repeating them as literals.

`IsValidEXT()` is not restated in C -- the route rebuilds the canonical value and asks it. That matters because the predicate has **seven arms and one of them depends on the shape**: a tube is a line with a radius and skips the parallel-axis test that a rectangle and a disc must pass. A reimplementation that applied the test to all three would reject a perfectly good tube, and asking the canonical object cannot get that wrong.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 36 and the layer-absent block. Each refusing arm is asserted on its own so one broken arm cannot hide behind another, and the shape-dependent arm is asserted with the case that isolates it: the *same* parallel axes read invalid as a rectangle, invalid as a disc, and **valid** as a tube. Both routes are asserted to succeed in the layer-absent build, tube exemption included. Break-proved: inverting the tube answer moves both CNAEXT trees; making the value pair refuse without the layer moves only the layer-absent tree.

rules.mapping:
`cna_area_light_brdf_table_*` over its own owned handle, with `CNA_AreaLightBrdfTerms` for the four numbers one entry carries and the two canonical defaults as macros, `static_assert`ed against the canonical constants.

The size and sample count are validated **as a pair and refused as a pair**, checked before construction so the message names both rather than being whichever half the canonical condition tested first. `evaluate` is the one route that mixes the two shapes: the sample count is **refused**, while its two float inputs are **clamped to bounds an eye would not guess** -- roughness to `[0.02, 1]`, not zero to one, because a perfect mirror has a lobe of zero width and no samples land in it, and the cosine to `[0.001, 1]` for the same reason at grazing angles.

The texture handle **borrows**: it keeps the table alive and releasing it releases only the handle.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 36. The clamps are asserted by **equality against the bound**, not by a range -- an out-of-range input must produce exactly what the bound produces, which is what distinguishes a clamp from a wider tolerance. Three bad size/sample pairs are refused with the handle left invalid, and the borrowed texture handle is released twice over to show the table keeps its texture.

rules.mapping:
`cna_area_light_shading_*` for the four pure functions and the GLSL, with the canonical `Quad` alias becoming a plain array of `CNA_AREA_LIGHT_QUAD_CORNER_COUNT` vectors, plus the forward effect's area-light setter that was waiting for both this and the table.

`quadOf` is shape-dependent in two ways and the binding preserves both: a disc scales its axes so a polygon matches the disc's area, and a **tube is billboarded** -- turned so its face points at the surface -- so a tube's quad depends on the point being lit while a rectangle's does not. `lobeScaleFor` clamps the roughness, squares it, and then **floors the result at `0.02`**, so a mirror still has a lobe with a width rather than a line.

**`setAreaLight` CLEARS on a degenerate light rather than refusing it**, which is what the canonical setter does -- a light with parallel axes or zero range would divide by zero in the form factor, and unsetting it is how the effect stays drawable. The route therefore succeeds, and the header says plainly that a successful call is not evidence a light was set; `cna_clustered_forward_effect_has_area_light` is. A *malformed structure* is a different thing and is refused.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 36. The quad is asserted for all three shapes and for the surface-dependence split -- a rectangle's quad is shown identical for two different surfaces, a tube's different -- so neither "ignores the shape" nor "billboards everything" survives. The clear-vs-refuse distinction is pinned by asserting the result code **and** `has_area_light` after a degenerate light, and again after a malformed one, which leaves the previous light in place. Break-proved: asserting the degenerate light was kept moves both CNAEXT trees.

rules.mapping:
`cna_particle_system_*` over its own owned handle, with `CNA_ParticleEmitterSettings` and `CNA_Particle` as versioned PODs and the two canonical constants as macros, `static_assert`ed against them.

**The distinguishing contract is that an unsustainable emission rate is not corrected on the way in.** `set_settings` assigns the struct whole and unvalidated, exactly as the canonical setter does; the clamp appears in `get_active_count` (rate × lifetime, rounded, capped at the capacity) and is reported by `is_emission_rate_clamped` (strictly greater than the capacity, so a rate that fills the system exactly is not clamped). A binding that clamped in the setter would look friendlier and would make `get_settings` lie about what it was given.

**`uses_compute` records what the last `update` did, not what the next one will do** -- it is written inside `update` and nowhere else, so `set_simulation_on_cpu_ext` does not change the answer until an update runs. The header says so, because asking it immediately after switching is the natural mistake.

Falling back to the CPU is a **success** path here, unlike GPU culling: the CPU path produces the same particles, only more slowly. Forcing it **carries the particles across** rather than restarting them, and setting the value it already has does nothing at all.

The two value initializers refuse without the engine layer, unlike `CNA_AreaLightEXT`'s and `CNA_ImageBasedLightEXT`'s -- the difference is where the canonical header lives, not whether the type is a POD.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 37 and the layer-absent block. The clamp contract is asserted from both ends: a 200/s rate on a 64-slot system reads back **unchanged** while the active count caps at 64 and the clamp flag is true; a sustainable rate gives the exact rounded product; a rate that fills the system exactly is asserted **not** clamped. The `uses_compute` ordering is asserted by stepping the simulation between the switch and the query. The carry-across is asserted by reading a particle before forcing the CPU and finding it unchanged after. The static hash is asserted deterministic *and* seed-sensitive, so a constant would fail. Break-proved in both directions.

rules.mapping:
`cna_instanced_renderer_ext_*` over its own owned handle. The mesh part is **borrowed** and retained by the resource, so releasing the part handle mid-frame cannot dangle.

**Whether instancing happens is a renderer question, and the answer is not a refusal.** With the fallback enabled a device without instancing draws each instance separately -- the same picture, more slowly. `did_last_draw_instance` and `get_last_draw_call_count` say which happened and what it cost, and like the particle system's compute flag they are records written by `draw` rather than predictions.

With the fallback **disabled**, drawing on such a renderer is refused -- and so is drawing through an effect that cannot carry a per-instance transform, because a per-instance world matrix has nowhere else to go. Both canonical refusals are `logic_error` and both arrive as `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`: the layer is present and the arguments are fine, this combination of renderer, setting and effect is not.

The two static declarations become element-copy plus stride routes rather than handles, because a shared static declaration has no owner to hand out. They exist because a caller building its own instance buffer must reproduce the layout **exactly**, and copying the elements is how it can check that rather than assume it.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 38. The instance declaration is asserted element by element -- four `Vector4`s sixteen bytes apart at `TextureCoordinate` usage indices one through four, stride sixty-four -- because "describe it identically" is the whole contract. The capacity is asserted **never to shrink** when fewer instances are uploaded, which is what makes a varying instance count allocation-free after the largest frame; zero instances is asserted to succeed. Both boolean setters refuse a non-canonical byte.

rules.mapping:
`cna_lod_group_ext_*` over its own owned handle, with `CNA_LodLevelEXT` for a level and `CNA_LodSelectionMode` at the canonical ordinals. The group needs **no graphics device** -- it is a list and a rule, and nothing in it touches one -- so its create route takes none.

**Index zero is always the finest level, in both selection modes**, and the group re-sorts on every change to keep it so: a distance threshold grows as detail falls and a pixel-radius threshold shrinks, so changing the mode reverses the order. That is why `set_selection_mode` also forgets the last selection. A binding that stored the mode without re-sorting would pass every single-mode assertion and silently invert the order for anyone who switched.

Several behaviours are answers rather than refusals: an empty group selects `-1`, a negative distance is **clamped to zero** (a camera behind the object is a position, not a mistake), a level may deliberately hold **no part**, and `projected_radius_pixels` answers the largest representable float at or behind the eye -- "as large as it gets", which picks the finest level rather than none. `set_hysteresis` floors at zero; `set_screen_space_parameters` is validated and refused as a **group**, with the field of view exclusive at both ends.

The group holds raw `ModelMeshPart` pointers, so the C layer remembers which handle each came from and hands **the caller's own handle** back rather than wrapping the pointer in a fresh one -- a fresh handle would be a second owner of something the group only borrows.
rules.tests: `EngineLayerSmoke.c` stage 38. The re-sort is asserted by adding three levels out of order, reading them back in `Distance` order, switching to `ScreenSpaceError`, and reading back the **reversed** order -- break-proved by asserting the unsorted order instead, which moves both CNAEXT trees. The screen-space triple is refused four ways and the previous projection shown unchanged after each; pi itself is asserted refused rather than clamped. Selection is asserted to hand back the caller's own part handle.
